# T008.1 — Port HelpPage MVC controller

## Summary

Ported all three generated HelpController actions to the side-by-side ASP.NET Core host. `/Help` and `/Help/Index` list discovered API endpoints; `/Help/Api/{apiId}` renders details; `/Help/ResourceModel?modelName=...` renders discoverable complex response/request models. Missing or unknown API IDs and model names render an Error view (HTTP 200), as characterized by the legacy controller's direct action results. The legacy project and source are unchanged.

## Changes (files and why)

- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Program.cs` — Register MVC API Explorer and the Help catalog; place the dedicated Help conventional route before the Home route without intercepting the attribute-routed API.
- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/HelpApiCatalog.cs` — Generate help entries, friendly IDs, parameter/response summaries and resource properties from the host's API Explorer; do not load System.Web or Web API 2.
- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Controllers/HelpController.cs` — Port Index, Api and ResourceModel with the characterized Error-view fallback; exclude documentation actions from API discovery.
- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Controllers/SampleController.cs` — Explicitly opt the already-characterized API endpoint into API Explorer metadata without changing its route or response handling.
- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Views/Help/{Index,Api,ResourceModel,Error}.cshtml` — Render encoded HTML for the API list, per-action parameters and responses, discovered model properties, and error fallback.
- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/wwwroot/Areas/HelpPage/HelpPage.css` — Copy the legacy Help stylesheet to its existing public URL.
- `DescopeSampleApp.IntegrationTests/HelpMvcTests.cs` — Offline WebApplicationFactory assertions for both index URLs, navigable API details, a test-only described response model, six missing/unknown input paths, the stylesheet and unchanged Home/Sample routing.

## Decisions (rationale and sources)

- Maintain the approved side-by-side migration with no IIS, YARP, legacy edits, or external HTTP. The legacy `Help/{action}/{apiId}` registration and HelpController direct-action characterization in T002.1 establish route and Error-view intent, but do not establish hosted response bytes.
- Use MVC API Explorer's `IApiDescriptionGroupCollectionProvider` rather than Web API 2's `HttpConfiguration`, as illustrated by [Microsoft's API-description group examples](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.openapi.openapidocumenttransformercontext.descriptiongroups?view=aspnetcore-10.0). MVC `AddMvcCore().AddApiExplorer()` and explicit API visibility provide descriptions while leaving `[ApiController]` disabled on SampleController. The test-only `HelpWidget` endpoint proves that ResourceModel can serve a real discovered complex type without inventing a production endpoint.
- Preserve the generated HelpPage title, introduction, three action names, `Help` route, useful request/response headings, stylesheet URL and missing-input Error-view behavior. Render MVC Razor with default HTML encoding. Only resource types that the catalog can actually render receive a link.
- **No byte-for-byte equivalence claim:** T002.1 used direct legacy action results and source inspection, not an IIS HTTP capture. The old Web API 2 sample generator, format-specific example bodies, XML documentation provider (disabled in the legacy HelpPageConfig), model-description annotations, legacy markup/layout and exact friendly IDs/content for arbitrary endpoints are not reproduced. Core API Explorer metadata may have different route casing, optional-segment representation, parameter type naming, documentation and response shapes; missing-input HTTP 200 is a new-host test expectation inferred from the legacy Error `ViewResult`, not a measured legacy HTTP status. The real application currently has no described complex API model, so positive resource rendering is covered using a test-only controller.

## Validation (commands and results)

- `msbuild -restore -p:RestorePackagesConfig=true -p:Configuration=Release -m -nologo -v:minimal` — pass; existing legacy NU1902 jQuery advisories and MSB3247 assembly conflict persist.
- `dotnet test --no-build -c Release` — pass; 74 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (23 net48 characterization and 51 net10 integration tests).
- Lint — none defined.

## Follow-ups and risks

- Compare the rendered HTML, generated links and status/headers against an actual legacy-host HelpPage capture if one becomes available; especially validate optional API IDs and the shape of any newly exposed models. Rich Web API 2 sample generation and annotations need a separately scoped port if consumers rely on them.
- Legacy NU1902 and MSB3247 warnings predate this task and were not suppressed or remediated here.
